question: When a weapon is submitted for forensic examination, the forensic physician must document the seal and labelling of the parcel before opening it, and must re-seal the exhibit in the same or equivalent container after examination with a fresh seal and signature.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Chain of custody integrity is essential for weapon exhibits to be admissible as evidence. The forensic physician must document the seal condition on receipt and re-seal the exhibit after examination. Failure to maintain chain of custody can invalidate the exhibit as evidence in court — a critical practical skill under FM14.10.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The chain of custody for medicolegal exhibits demands: (1) documentation of the intact seal and labelling on receipt, (2) careful opening without destroying seals if possible, (3) systematic examination with full documentation, and (4) re-sealing with the examiner's own seal and signature. Any break in this procedure can render the exhibit legally inadmissible or open to challenge in court.
